sources.title: The Sons of Israel or God? Deuteronomy 32:8
sources.edition: TheTorah.com article
sources.inspected_scope: Report of the Göttingen LXX reading and Papyrus 848
sources.limitations: Secondary report; the Göttingen edition itself was not inspected. Added by the independent reviewer.

row_summaries.summary: Only KTU 1.1 and 1.3 could be inspected in a line-numbered edition (Steinberger). They show El naming Yam at a feast and the formula 'sons of Athirat', but the core loci (pḫr mˁd in 1.2 I; šbˁm bn aṯrt in 1.4 VI) remain not_checked, and the vocalized 'puḫru môʿidi' should be dropped.
Reference widened to 82:1-8; council term and members attested in MAM but their 'divine' sense is a reading (JPS 1917: 'congregation of God', 'judges', 'godlike beings').
All fields attested in MAM and JPS 1917; only 'kol' ('all') added to the term.
Reference extended to 1:6-12; 2:1-7; 'wager' is not in the text (challenge and permission); 'Accuser' is a gloss.

MT reads bənê yiśrāʾēl; 'sons of God' rests on 4QDeutj and the Göttingen LXX choice, both known here only from secondary sources (majority LXX: ἀγγέλων θεοῦ); 'bənê ʾēl' unsupported; 'one over each nation' is inference.
Seraphim stand above him and are not described as a council; 'high and lifted up' modifies the throne; lānû ('for us') is attested but 'council plural' is interpretation.

The Tablet of Destinies is not granted by the assembly (Tiamat gives it to Kingu; Marduk seizes it); the assembly gives kingship, insignia and weapon. Reference narrowed to III/IV, with Tablet VI pending a modern edition; 'puḫur ilāni' is attested but first of Tiamat's assembly.

Anu is king and Enlil is counsellor; Enlil convenes and speaks, but 'presides' is not textual. puḫrum is confirmed in SEAL. The flood oath is in an MB witness, and Enki's pre-flood objection (II H 9–16) is restored, with his explicit criticism coming after the flood.

'Lord of Spirits' removed (Similitudes only, per Charles p. 66); Great Glory attested at 14:20; reference narrowed to chs 9-10, 12-16; text says God 'needed no counsellor' (14:22), so court not deliberative council.

Rieken et al.'s CTH 344 edition shows a dynastic succession by combat and a proem invoking primeval gods as listeners, but no assembly or council. Recommend removing the row from a divine-council index, or reclassifying it as a succession myth.
'Council in heaven' is not in Moses 4 or Abraham 3 (study-aid/teaching label); nearest scripture is D&C 121:32 'Council of the Eternal God'; 'debates' overstates an offer-and-choice scene.

The noun ἀγορή is in Il. 20.4/20.16 only; Book 4 uses the verb ἠγορόωντο. Apollo is not named in either range, Athena is silent, and the Book 4 outcome is breaking the truce, with Troy's sack conceded to Hera.

Checked only against an unattributed web translation, so most fields are qualified. Geb is not named, 'eighty years' is the case's time before the tribunal, and the c. 1147 BCE date traces to an uncited Wikipedia infobox. psḏt and the papyrus locators still need Gardiner 1931 or Lichtheim.

Ovid writes concilium (1.167), presided over by Jupiter. The gods assent to destroying humankind (1.244–245), not to a flood. Jupiter chooses the flood alone afterwards (1.253–261), and the commoner deities are not seated.
rökstóla, regin and ginnheilög goð are confirmed at Vsp 6, 9, 23, 25 (Bellows 6, 9, 24, 25). The function should add st. 25 and read st. 23 as a tribute debate. Odin (Allfather) presides in Gylf. 14.

The scene is in the Ki-ur (lines 54–64), not the Ekur. 'ukkin' and 'Anuna' do not occur in the composition; the actors are 'the fifty great gods and the seven gods who decide destinies', who have Enlil arrested; he leaves the city as ritually impure 'in accordance with what had been decided', with no narrated trial.
The council is Ganguli Sec. XVII = CE 1.15.5–13. devasabhā/sabhā does not occur in the critical text, which says mantrayitum … samāgamya. No presider is named: Nārāyaṇa addresses Brahmā.

observations.proposed_value: KTU 1.1 IV 1–32 (El's feast and naming of Yam; fragmentary); KTU 1.2 I (Yam's envoys before the gods' assembly) and KTU 1.4 VI (seventy sons of Athirat) still to be checked in a named edition
observations.note: Whole-cycle reference is too broad. Only KTU 1.1 and 1.3 could be opened in a line-numbered edition. In 1.1 IV the scene is fragmentary: Smith restores lp[ḫr.il] at l. 3 with a question mark; the words 'only a guess' in Steinberger's n. 9 are Smith's, about qb[ṣ] in l. 2. The key assembly passage (1.2 I) was not inspected.

observations.old_value: puḫru môʿidi / pḫr mʿd (“the assembled council”); bn ilm (“sons of El”)
observations.proposed_value: pḫr mˁd (consonantal; locus KTU 1.2 I to be confirmed); bn ilm (locus to be confirmed). Drop the vocalized 'puḫru môʿidi' from the term column
observations.locator: KTU 1.2 I (not opened); KTU 1.3 V 18; KTU 1.1 IV 2–3 n. 9
observations.note: No open line-numbered edition of KTU 1.2 I was found, so pḫr mˁd is not confirmed. Ugaritic script is consonantal, so 'puḫru môʿidi' is a modern vocalization (Akkadian-style) and does not appear in the text. In the files inspected, bn . ilm occurs only in the reconstruction column at 1.3 V 18 ([d . bn . ilm . m]t, Mot), and pḫr only in Smith's tentative restoration at 1.1 IV 3.

observations.old_value: El, the aged father of the gods
observations.proposed_value: El (lṭpn il dpid) speaks and names Yam in the inspected scene; El's presidency over the assembly in KTU 1.2 I not checked
observations.note: In 1.1 IV 13–14 'wyˁn lṭpn il d[pid] … šm bny yw' (the Kindly One, El, answers: the name of my son is Yw); l. 4 'ṣḥ il' (El calls). This shows El speaking at a feast (drinking, l. 9–10). The text does not call him presiding, and 'the aged father' is an epithet that the inspected lines do not print.

observations.old_value: The sons of El / the seventy sons of Athirat
observations.proposed_value: The gods / the sons of Athirat (bn aṯrt); 'seventy sons of Athirat' (šbˁm bn aṯrt, cited for KTU 1.4 VI) not checked
observations.note: 1.3 V 3–4 reads lytn . bt . lbˁl . kilm / [wḥẓ]r . kbn . aṯrt, which glosses as 'no house for Baal like the gods, [no court] like the sons of Athirat'. This attests 'sons of Athirat' as a group of gods. It is a set formula, not an assembly scene. The number seventy was not seen in any inspected file. 'Sons of El' (bn il/ilm) is not confirmed (see council_term).

observations.old_value: El presides while the assembly debates and confers kingship (Baal, Yam, Mot contend)
observations.proposed_value: El names Yam (his son Yw) at a divine feast, and the restored text has Baal driven from his royal throne. That the assembly 'debates and confers kingship' is not shown in the inspected scope
observations.note: In the inspected text, kingship is conferred by El's naming speech, not by an assembly vote. The throne clause at l. 24 is Steinberger's reconstruction. The Baal–Yam–Mot contest spans the cycle, but the 1.2 I assembly and the 1.6 I Athtar episode were not inspected.

observations.proposed_value: Deuteronomy 32:8–9

observations.proposed_value: Deuteronomy (Song of Moses)

observations.proposed_value: bənê ʾĕlōhîm (“sons of God”) in 4QDeutj as reported by Hendel; LXX: υἱῶν θεοῦ adopted by the Göttingen edition (reported), majority text ἀγγέλων θεοῦ; MT reads bənê yiśrāʾēl (בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל)
observations.note: MT inspected: בני ישראל, JPS 1917 "children of Israel". 4QDeutj reading and Göttingen υἱῶν θεοῦ known only from secondary discussion; DJD XIV not opened. The common LXX text inspected prints ἀγγέλων Θεοῦ. "bənê ʾēl" not supported by any inspected source - it is a scholarly reconstruction; drop it or label as conjecture. Tov (TheTorah.com) independently reports that Wevers adopts 'sons of God', citing Papyrus 848.

observations.note: Commission speech continues to 6:13; 6:1-8 covers the scene.

observations.old_value: Isaiah (throne vision)
observations.proposed_value: Isaiah (throne vision)

observations.old_value: The seraphim before the throne
observations.proposed_value: No council term; śərāpîm ʿōmədîm mimmaʿal lô (שְׂרָפִים עֹמְדִים מִמַּעַל לוֹ, “seraphim standing above him”)
observations.note: Seraphim stand "above Him" (JPS 1917), not "before the throne"; they praise (v.3) and one purifies the prophet (vv.6-7). They are never addressed or described as deliberating; council status is interpretive.

observations.old_value: Yahweh, “high and lifted up”
observations.proposed_value: ʾĂdōnāy sitting on a throne “high and lifted up” (6:1); “the King, YHWH of hosts” (6:5)
observations.note: Text names ʾĂdōnāy in v.1 (Yahweh in v.3, 5). "High and lifted up" (rām wənissāʾ) qualifies the throne in JPS 1917 and by agreement (the indefinite adjectives follow the indefinite kissēʾ; ʾĂdōnāy is definite); the row attaches it to Yahweh.

observations.old_value: The seraphim
observations.proposed_value: The seraphim (6:2, 6); no other attendants named

observations.old_value: Commissioning — “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” (the council plural)
observations.proposed_value: Commissioning — “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us (lānû)?” (6:8); the first-person plural is read by some as addressed to a council
observations.note: לָנוּ ("for us") is attested wording; "council plural" is an interpretation, not stated in the text.

observations.old_value: Tablets II–VI
observations.proposed_value: Tablet III 1–66, 109–138 (Anšar sends his message; Marduk's condition; the gods gather before Anšar and decree his fate); IV 1–34 (dais, kingship, insignia, weapon); Tablet VI assemblies (Qingu's trial, Esagila banquet, bow, names): locators to be set from a modern edition
observations.note: Narrowed from 'Tablets II–VI'. The line numbers are King's. Tablet VI is almost entirely missing in King 1902, and eBL (API timeout) and the Lambert translation hosts were unreachable, so modern-edition locators for II and VI are not given.

observations.old_value: puḫur ilāni (“the assembly of the gods”)
observations.proposed_value: puḫru 'assembly' (III 60/118, IV 15 ina puḫri); ina puḫur ilāni 'in the assembly of the gods' (Tiamat's speech to Kingu, I c. 136 and repeats; Anu and the bow, King's Tablet V fragment; VII 13); assembly hall Upšukkinakku (III 61)
observations.locator: King I c. 134–138; III 60–61; IV 15; King's Tablet V fragment (K. 3,449[a], OCR); VII 13
observations.note: The forms are confirmed only through King's 1902 transliteration, read through OCR. 'puḫur ilāni' is attested, but its first uses are for Tiamat's counter-assembly that exalts Kingu. In the Anšar/Marduk scenes King prints puḫru/puḫri. The modern-edition wording was not checked.

observations.old_value: Anšar, then Marduk (elected)
observations.proposed_value: Anšar (the gods are summoned and 'enter before Anšar', III 131); the gods enthrone Marduk, who is acclaimed king (IV 29); Marduk's later presiding (VI) not checked
observations.note: 'Elected' compresses IV 1–29. The gods set up a dais and test his word, and then 'Marduk is king' (Marduk-ma šarru, IV 29). In the King fragment, Anu raises the bow ina puḫur ilāni. That fragment is VI in modern editions and was not checked there.

observations.old_value: The great gods (the Anunnaki)
observations.proposed_value: The great gods 'who decree fate', including Laḫmu and Laḫamu, gathered before Anšar (the Igigi lament, III 126); designation of the assembly as 'the Anunnaki' (VI) not checked
observations.note: King III 130: 'the great gods, all of them, who decree [fate]'. In the inspected Anšar scenes 'Anunnaki' names Tiamat's host in the Kingu speech (I c. 137), not the assembly that empowers Marduk.

observations.old_value: The assembly grants Marduk kingship and the Tablet of Destinies to fight Tiamat
observations.proposed_value: The assembly decrees Marduk's fate and gives him kingship over the whole universe, with throne, sceptre, palû and an unrivalled weapon, to fight Tiamat. Marduk later takes the Tablet(s) of Destinies from Kingu; the assembly does not grant them
observations.locator: King III 136–138; IV 14, 29–31; Tablet of Destinies: I c. 137, IV c. 119–122
observations.note: Correction: Tiamat gives the Tablet(s) of Destiny to Kingu (King I c. 137), and Marduk seizes them after the battle (King IV c. 119–122, p. 75). The assembly gives kingship (šarrūtu kiššat kal gimrēti, IV 14) and the throne, sceptre and palû (IV 30) and the weapon (IV 31). Line numbers are King's and approximate where the OCR breaks.

observations.proposed_value: https://www.wheelofheaven.world/library/enuma-elish/
observations.note: A project library page exists (HTTP 200). It is a partial King 1902 extraction that lacks Tablet III, the main assembly tablet. Linking it is the editor's choice.

observations.old_value: Tablets I–III
observations.proposed_value: I 7–18, 101–144, 172–226 (offices; assembly on the Igigi strike; creation of man); II Seg. A 5–15, E 9–16, E 67–74, G 49q–u, G 63–97, H 1–28; III C1 iii 36′–54′, v 39″–45″, vi 5–27, vi 41′–44′
observations.locator: SEAL I; SEAL II (synoptic segments); SEAL III Sippar C1
observations.note: Reference narrowed to the located passage. The assembly scenes are located in SEAL. II G 49q–u (flood oath) survives only in X-MB, a Middle Babylonian witness. These locators match the project's flood procedural comparison (A1/A2).

observations.old_value: puḫrum (“the assembly”)
observations.proposed_value: puḫrum ('assembly'; OB pu-úḫ-ri(-im), e.g. ina puḫri īpulū anna, I 218; ana puḫrim ša ilī, II G 64/66; III C1 iii 36′, vi 27); later witnesses ina puḫur kala ilī (X-MB, II G 49r), Enlil ištakan puḫuršu (NA, II A 5)
observations.locator: SEAL I A iv 10; SEAL II C0 i 8–12, X-MB rev. i 45, S+T+-NA iv 37; SEAL III C1 iii 36′, vi 27
observations.note: The term is confirmed in printed transliteration at several loci. The bound OB form is pu-úḫ-ri-im. 'ina puḫur kala ilī' is Middle Babylonian.

observations.old_value: Enlil
observations.proposed_value: Anu is king (šarru); Enlil, their counsellor (mālikšunu), convenes and addresses the assembly; Anu swears first in the flood oath
observations.locator: SEAL I 7–8 (A i 7–8: a-nu a-bu-šu-nu šarru / māliksunu qurādu Enlil); I 101–104; II A 5–6, E 67–68, G 49q–u
observations.note: The text does not give Enlil the office of presiding. Anu sits as king of heaven, and 'Enlil arose and the case was presented' (I 101–104). Enlil summons the assembly (II A 5 var., E 67) and calls for the oath (G 49q–s), and 'Anu had sworn first; then Enlil swore, his sons with him' (G 49t–u, X-MB). In III Nintu blames both Anu ('who calls the shots', C1 iii 51′, v 39″) and Enlil. SEAL's commentary to I 8 notes that, Enlil usually being king of the gods, the scribe may play on malku 'ruler' in his counsellor title.

observations.old_value: The great gods; Enki (Ea) dissents
observations.proposed_value: The great gods / the great Anunnaki (Anu, Enlil, Enki/Ea, Ninurta, Ennugi named in office; Enlil's sons swear); Nintu/Mami speaks in the assembly; Enki (Ea) objects to the oath
observations.note: 'Enki dissents' is attested only in part. A speaker proposes to bind 'prince Enki' by oath (H 9–10); SEAL's commentary presumes Mama is the speaker, as these lines repeat part of her speech in I 240–243a, and notes that Enki's answer (H 11ff.) is addressed to the assembly. Enki asks 'Why will you bind me with an oath? … Can I lay my hands on my own people?' (H 13–14). H 9–10 are heavily restored (B vii, D vii).

observations.old_value: The assembly decrees the flood under oath — a decision Enki argues against
observations.proposed_value: The assembly decides the human-creation plan (I 218 'Yes!'), then a series of plagues (II), and then the flood under oath (II G 49q–u, X-MB). Enki contests the oath before the flood (II H 9–16, restored) and criticizes the unconsidered flood afterwards (III C1 vi 18–26)
observations.note: The baseline compresses the timing. The pre-flood oath is in the MB witness, and III C1 vi 7–8 recalls 'All we great Anunnaki decided together on oath'. Enki's objection is restoration-dependent. His later protest comes after the flood. The gods already decide on oath in the plague section (II E 11–12 // E 29–30; Enlil at G 28–29), so deciding by oath is attested outside the MB witness; the flood-specific oath is MB only. In III C1 vi 20–22 the phrase 'without deliberation' is restored.

observations.old_value: https://www.wheelofheaven.world/library/atrahasis-woh/
observations.proposed_value: https://www.wheelofheaven.world/library/atrahasis-woh/
observations.locator: atrahasis-woh; see procedural-comparison 'Passage attribution requiring follow-up'
observations.note: The link resolves (HTTP 200). The project's locators (ATRA-WOH-III:vi) do not align with SEAL C1 numbering, so cite SEAL locators in the dataset, not the project's.

"6-16; 14" overlaps itself; chs 6-8 narrate the descent, not the court. Court scenes: archangels' petition ch. 9, sentences ch. 10, Enoch's commission and throne vision chs 12-16. 10:5-16 and 12-13 only partly inspected.

observations.old_value: Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch)
observations.proposed_value: Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch)

observations.old_value: The “Holy Ones” / the heavenly host before the throne
observations.proposed_value: “The holy ones (of heaven)” (9:3; 14:23, 25); “ten thousand times ten thousand” before him (14:22)
observations.note: English of Charles' translation; 9:3 phrase is in Charles' half-brackets (text-critical marking; lost in Greek through homoioteleuton per note). Ethiopic/Greek terms not checked. Note 14:22: "yet He needed no counsellor" - the text itself denies counsel.

observations.old_value: The Great Glory / the Lord of Spirits
observations.proposed_value: The Great Glory (14:20); the Most High, the Holy and Great One (10:1); the Holy Great One (14:1)
observations.note: "Great Glory" attested at 14:20 (and in a Greek fragment at 9:3 per Charles' note). "Lord of Spirits" does not belong here: Charles p. 66 lists it among divine names "found only in 37-71" (Similitudes). Remove it.

observations.old_value: The Holy Ones; the Watchers (rebel members who descend)
observations.proposed_value: The holy ones before the throne; the archangels Michael, Uriel, Raphael and Gabriel (9:1); the Watchers of heaven (14:1; 15:2), who left the high, holy and eternal heaven (15:3)
observations.note: Archangels added as named members. "Watchers of heaven" at 15:2 is half-bracketed in Charles.

observations.old_value: The heavenly court; the archangels petition; judgment on the Watchers
observations.proposed_value: Petition by the archangels to the Most High (9:1–11); sentences on Azazel, Semjaza and the Watchers (10); Watchers' petition via Enoch rejected (13–16)
observations.note: Court and judgment attested. No deliberation: God decides alone and "needed no counsellor" (14:22). "Heavenly court" fits; "council" overstates.

observations.old_value: CTH 344
observations.proposed_value: CTH 344, Expl. A (KUB 33.120 + …) Vs. I 1–7 (proem: the primeval gods are called to listen); Vs. I 8 ff. (§§2–6: Alalu → Anu → Kumarbi succession)
observations.note: Reference narrowed to the located passage. Running line 9 ('Formerly, in earlier years, Alalu was king in heaven') = A Vs. I 8. Running line 25 (Anu's nine years) = A Vs. I 18.

observations.old_value: The gods of heaven, in dynastic succession
observations.proposed_value: No council or assembly term in the preserved text; the primeval gods (karuiliyaš DINGIR.MEŠ-iš) are addressed as an audience ('may they listen')
observations.locator: CTH 344 §§1–2 (A Vs. I 1–7); full translation searched
observations.note: 'The gods of heaven, in dynastic succession' describes the plot, not a council term. The proem is an invocation, not a deliberating body.

observations.old_value: The reigning sky-king (Alalu → Anu → Kumarbi → Teshub)
observations.proposed_value: The reigning king in heaven: Alalu, then Anu, then Kumarbi (each served by the next); the Storm-god's kingship is only fragmentarily preserved
observations.note: No one presides over an assembly. Each king sits on the throne while the next god bows and serves drink, and kingship passes by combat. Teshub's accession is fragmentary (§19'' 'Make [ … ] king!'; §20'' 'who now fights against me?').

observations.old_value: The divine dynasty
observations.proposed_value: The divine dynasty (Alalu, Anu, Kumarbi, the Storm-god), with Ea and other gods as actors in fragmentary scenes
observations.note: This is not an assembly membership.

observations.old_value: The succession of divine kingship in heaven
observations.proposed_value: The succession of kingship in heaven by combat (Alalu deposed by Anu, Anu by Kumarbi), with later fragmentary plotting over Kumarbi and the Storm-god. No council deliberation is attested
observations.note: In §19'' a 'we' voice says 'we destroy …' and 'Make [ … ] king!', but the speakers and setting are lost. These lines do not establish a council.
There is no project library book, so the empty value stands.

observations.old_value: Moses 4:1–4; Abraham 3:22–28
observations.proposed_value: Moses 4:1–4; Abraham 3:22–28; cf. D&C 121:32
observations.note: Existing ranges show the scene; D&C 121:32 is the scriptural source of "Council of the Eternal God".

observations.old_value: Book of Moses / Book of Abraham
observations.proposed_value: Book of Moses / Book of Abraham
observations.note: Pearl of Great Price.

observations.old_value: The “council in heaven”; the “noble and great ones”
observations.proposed_value: No council term in Moses 4 or Abraham 3; “the noble and great ones” (Abr 3:22); scripture elsewhere: “the Council of the Eternal God of all other gods before this world was” (D&C 121:32); “council in heaven” is a later teaching / study-aid label; deliberation wording: “the Gods took counsel among themselves” (Abr 4:26)
observations.note: "Council" does not occur in the scripture text of Moses 4 or Abraham 3; "Council in Heaven" appears only as a Topical Guide cross-reference in footnotes. Joseph Smith's sermons not inspected.

observations.old_value: God the Father
observations.proposed_value: God (Abr 3:23, “the Lord”, 3:27); “the Lord God”, addressed as “Father” (Moses 4:1–2)
observations.note: "God the Father" is a fair synthesis.

observations.old_value: The premortal spirits / the noble and great ones
observations.proposed_value: The intelligences / spirits organized before the world, among them the noble and great ones (Abr 3:22–23); one “like unto God” (3:24); the Beloved Son and Satan (Moses 4:1–2)

observations.old_value: The premortal council debates the plan and the choice of a Redeemer
observations.proposed_value: The Lord asks “Whom shall I send?”; two volunteer and the first is chosen; Satan, offering to redeem all mankind for God's honor, rebels and is cast down
observations.note: Text shows offer and choice, not a debate; "choosing of a Redeemer" is the chapter heading's (editorial) wording. Moses 4:1 has Satan offer to "redeem all mankind".
Both scenes are divine assemblies. 4.1–72 runs from the session to Zeus's order to Athena. 20.4–30 runs from Themis's summons to Zeus's speech.

observations.old_value: ἀγορή (agorḗ, ‘assembly of the gods’)
observations.proposed_value: ἀγορή (θεοὺς ἀγορὴν δὲ καλέσσαι, Il. 20.4, 20.16); in Book 4 the verb ἠγορόωντο ‘were holding assembly’ (4.1)
observations.note: The noun ἀγορή occurs at 20.4 and 20.16, not in 4.1–72. Book 4 uses the verb ἠγορόωντο (Murray: 'were holding assembly'). θόωκος is not in either passage.

observations.old_value: Zeus
observations.proposed_value: Zeus
observations.note: Book 4: the gods sit beside Zeus and he opens the question. Book 20: Zeus has Themis summon the assembly and states its purpose.

observations.old_value: Hera, Athena, Poseidon, Apollo, Themis, and the Olympian gods
observations.proposed_value: Book 4: Zeus, Hera, Athena (silent), Hebe pouring nectar, the gods; Book 20: Themis (summoner), Poseidon, all rivers except Oceanus, the nymphs, the gods
observations.note: Apollo is not named in either cited range. Aphrodite is only mentioned by Zeus (4.10). Book 20 says no river except Oceanus and no nymph stayed away.

observations.old_value: The gods sit in assembly; Zeus raises whether to end or renew the war, Hera and Athena argue, and the destruction of Troy is resolved
observations.proposed_value: Book 4: Zeus asks whether to renew the war or make peace (4.14–19). Hera objects while Athena stays silent (4.22–24). Zeus concedes Troy's sack to Hera (4.37). On her proposal he sends Athena to make the Trojans break the oaths (4.62–72). Book 20: Zeus releases the gods to join either side (20.22–25)
observations.note: Only Hera argues; Athena 'held her peace' (Murray). The 4.1–72 assembly ends with Athena sent to provoke the breach of the truce (the breach itself follows later in Book 4), with the sack conceded in principle. The Book 20 assembly is not covered by the old value.

observations.old_value: Chester Beatty I (20th Dynasty, c. 1147 BCE)
observations.proposed_value: P. Chester Beatty I, recto (the Contendings), per Gardiner 1931; dated by Gardiner to the reign of Ramesses V, 'roughly … 1160 B.C.'
observations.note: Gardiner places the papyrus in Ramesses V's reign, 'roughly dated to 1160 B.C.' The baseline's 'c. 1147 BCE' traces to an uncited Wikipedia infobox and is not supported by the inspected edition. Absolute Egyptian dates depend on the chronology used; Gardiner's is reported as his.

observations.old_value: The Contendings of Horus and Seth (Papyrus Chester Beatty I)
observations.proposed_value: The Contendings of Horus and Seth (Papyrus Chester Beatty I)
observations.locator: Gardiner 1931, title page and ch. I
observations.note: Identification confirmed in Gardiner's edition.

observations.old_value: the Great Ennead — psḏt (‘the Nine’)
observations.proposed_value: the Ennead (psḏt); a few times 'the great Ennead'
observations.note: Gardiner: "'Ennead' is the accepted English equivalent of the Egyptian psḏt" and "in our tale the Ennead is a few times named 'the great Ennead'". The term is confirmed through Gardiner's note, not through a hieroglyphic transcription inspected here.

observations.old_value: Re-Horakhty (the Lord of All)
observations.proposed_value: The sun-god, rendered 'the Master of the Universe' by Gardiner ('Universal Lord' in the web translation), also named Pre-Harakhti and Atum; he stands outside the Ennead
observations.note: Gardiner: 'The sun-god is conceived of as standing outside [the Ennead]'. 'Lord of All' (baseline) matches neither inspected rendering.

observations.old_value: Thoth, Isis, Geb, Neith, Atum, Shu
observations.proposed_value: Shu, Thoth, Onuris, Banebdjedet, Isis (litigant's mother) and the Ennead; Neith and Osiris are consulted by letter
observations.note: Geb is not named in the story; he appears only in Gardiner's list of the Heliopolitan Ennead (p. 14 n. 3) and in the web page's glossary. Neith takes part only by letter, from Sais. Atum is a name of the presiding god, not a separate member.

observations.old_value: A divine tribunal adjudicates the eighty-year succession dispute over Osiris's throne between Horus and Seth
observations.proposed_value: A divine tribunal adjudicates the dispute between Horus and Seth over Osiris's office. The text says the case had been before the tribunal for eighty years
observations.note: 'eighty years … in the tribunal' occurs twice: in the letter to Neith and in Horus's complaint. This makes it the length of the case, not of the dispute generally. Gardiner gives both locators: 'before the tribunal (2, 13; 13, 12)'.

observations.old_value: Metamorphoses 1.163–252
observations.proposed_value: Metamorphoses 1.163–252 (flood choice 1.253–261)
observations.note: The council runs from its summons (1.167) to Jupiter's promise of a new race (1.250–252). The flood itself is chosen just after, at 1.253–261.

observations.old_value: concilium (deorum)
observations.proposed_value: concilium (conciliumque vocat, 1.167); the members are called superi (1.177, 1.196)
observations.note: Ovid writes concilium alone; 'deorum' does not qualify concilium; the word occurs at 1.171 in another construction. More: 'he convened a council'.

observations.old_value: Jupiter
observations.proposed_value: Jupiter
observations.note: He sits higher than the rest, leaning on an ivory sceptre (1.178), and silences the assembly (1.205–208).

observations.old_value: The assembled gods — the great gods and the commoner deities
observations.proposed_value: The superi from the noble halls of the potentes caelicolae (1.171–177). The plebs lives elsewhere (1.173), and demigods, nymphs, fauns and satyrs are spoken of as outside heaven (1.192–195)
observations.note: The passage sets the commoner deities ('plebs habitat diversa locis') apart from the noble gods' quarter. It does not seat them in the council, so 'commoner deities' as members is not supported.

observations.old_value: Jupiter convenes the gods, denounces Lycaon and humankind, and the assembly assents to his resolve to destroy the human race by flood
observations.proposed_value: Jupiter convenes the gods, tells the Lycaon story and announces a sentence already sworn: the human race must perish (1.188–191, 1.240–243 'sic stat sententia'). Some gods approve aloud and others assent (1.244–245), but all grieve and ask about the future (1.246–249), and he promises a new race (1.250–252). He chooses the flood afterwards, alone (1.253–261)
observations.note: The gods assent to destroying humankind, not to a flood. The flood is chosen after the council, in place of thunderbolts. More: 'some approved the words … others gave assent'.

observations.old_value: Völuspá st. 6, 9, 23–25; Gylfaginning ch. 14
observations.proposed_value: Völuspá st. 6, 9, 23, 25 (Codex Regius order; Bellows 6, 9, 24, 25); Gylfaginning ch. 14
observations.note: The rökstóla refrain occurs in four stanzas: 6, 9, 23 and 25. Stanza 24 is the war itself. Bellows transposes MS 23/24, so his numbers are 6, 9, 24 and 25.

observations.old_value: rökstólar (‘seats of counsel’); the regin / ginnheilög goð
observations.proposed_value: rökstólar (acc. pl. rökstóla); regin öll; ginnheilög goð. Translations: 'assembly-seats' (Bellows), 'seats of judgment' (Brodeur)
observations.locator: Vsp 6, 9, 23, 25 ('Þá gengu regin öll á rökstóla, ginnheilög goð, ok um þat gættusk')
observations.note: All three terms are printed at each refrain. The gloss 'seats of counsel' is the project's own; neither inspected translator uses it.

observations.old_value: The regin collectively; Odin in the Prose Edda
observations.proposed_value: Völuspá: the regin collectively (no presider). Gylfaginning 14: Allfather (Odin), who set up the rulers and has the high-seat beside their twelve seats
observations.note: Brodeur: Allfather 'established rulers, and bade them ordain fates with him … the high-seat which Allfather himself has'.

observations.old_value: The Æsir (the ruling powers)
observations.proposed_value: Völuspá: regin öll / ginnheilög goð. Gylfaginning 14: the rulers Allfather established (twelve seats)
observations.note: The council stanzas say regin/goð, not æsir. St. 23 has the council debate whether the æsir should pay tribute, which implies the Vanir also have a claim to it. 'Æsir' as the members is an inference.

observations.old_value: The gods take their seats of counsel — ordering time, resolving to fashion the dwarves, and deliberating the Æsir–Vanir war
observations.proposed_value: The gods take the rökstólar to name night, day and the times for counting years (st. 6), to decide who should shape the dwarves (st. 9), to debate whether the æsir pay tribute or all gods share worship (st. 23), and to find who mixed the air with poison and gave Óðr's maid to the giants (st. 25). Gylf. 14: rulers ordain fates and plan the town
observations.note: The old value leaves out st. 25 (the wall-builder / Freyja episode). St. 23 is about tribute or shared worship after the war, not the war itself.

observations.old_value: ETCSL 1.2.1 (the Ki-ur / Ekur judgment scene)
observations.proposed_value: ETCSL 1.2.1, lines 54–64 (Enlil seized in the Ki-ur)
observations.note: Reference narrowed to the located passage. The scene is set in the Ki-ur (ki-ur3-ra, 54–55, 58), not 'the Ekur'. E-kur occurs only in Nuska's title, 'master builder of the E-kur' (35–53).

observations.old_value: ukkin (the assembly) — ‘the fifty great gods’ and ‘the seven who decree the fates’ (the Anunna)
observations.proposed_value: No assembly term in the passage. The groups are named dijir gal-gal 50-ne-ne 'the fifty great gods' and dijir nam-tar-ra 7-na-ne-ne 'the seven gods who decide destinies'
observations.note: 'ukkin' does not occur anywhere in the ETCSL 1.2.1 composite, and neither does 'Anuna' (a-nun). Both are supplied in the baseline. The passage names the two groups but uses no assembly term.

observations.old_value: The assembly collectively (Enlil is the defendant, not the presider)
observations.proposed_value: None named: 'the fifty great gods and the seven gods who decide destinies' are the subjects who have Enlil arrested; Enlil is the one seized
observations.note: The baseline's point that Enlil is not the presider holds. 'The assembly collectively' adds an institution the text does not name.

observations.old_value: The fifty great gods; the seven Anunna who decree the fates
observations.proposed_value: The fifty great gods; the seven gods who decide destinies
observations.note: 'The seven Anunna' is not in the text: 7-na is the numeral seven with a suffix. Do not gloss 'the seven who decree the fates' as 'Anunna'.

observations.old_value: The divine assembly at Nippur seizes, judges, and banishes Enlil as ritually impure for defiling Ninlil
observations.proposed_value: In the Ki-ur, the fifty great gods and the seven who decide destinies have Enlil arrested. Enlil, 'the ritually impure' (u2-zug4), leaves the city 'in accordance with what had been decided' (2 mss.: 'Enlil, ritually impure, leave the city!')
observations.note: 'At Nippur' is supported (lines 1–12, 59–60); 'judges' and 'for defiling Ninlil' go beyond the text. No trial or verdict speech is narrated. The decision is reported impersonally (nij2-nam-ce3 nam mu-un-tar-ra, 61–62), and the link to the act with Ninlil is implicit from the sequence.
There is no project library book for this composition, so the empty value stands.

observations.old_value: Adi Parva, Sections XVII–XVIII (the churning of the ocean of milk)
observations.proposed_value: Ganguli Adi Parva Section XVII (council); XVIII (churning). Critical edition 1.15.5–13 (council), 1.16 (churning)
observations.note: The conclave on Meru is in Section XVII alone (CE 1.15.5–13). Section XVIII is the churning, with later consultations of Vishnu and Brahmā at Mandara and mid-churning.

observations.old_value: devasabhā / sabhā (the conclave of the celestials)
observations.proposed_value: Sanskrit: mantrayitum ārabdhās tatrāsīnā … samāgamya ('seated there, having assembled, they began to deliberate', CE 1.15.10). Ganguli: 'held a conclave', 'the celestial assembly'
observations.note: Neither devasabhā nor sabhā occurs in CE 1.15.5–13. The text uses mantr- (deliberate) and samāgam- (assemble). The vulgate text behind Ganguli was not inspected. 'conclave' is Ganguli's English.

observations.old_value: Brahmā, with Nārāyaṇa (Vishnu) as counselor
observations.proposed_value: Not stated. Nārāyaṇa speaks to Brahmā (nārāyaṇo devo brahmāṇam idam abravīt); Brahmā is the one addressed
observations.note: No presider is named. In the rejected starred line CE *262 the gods and daityas approach Brahmā; it does not make him presider. Later, in Sec. XVIII, the gods come to Vishnu and Brahmā 'who were sitting'.

observations.old_value: The devas, assembled on Mount Meru
observations.proposed_value: All the gods (surāḥ sarve, divaukasaḥ) on the summit of Meru
observations.note: Ganguli: 'all the mighty celestials sat them down and held a conclave'. Brahmā and Nārāyaṇa are present.

observations.old_value: The celestials sit in conclave on Meru; Nārāyaṇa counsels Brahmā and they resolve to churn the ocean of milk for the amrita (the nectar of immortality)
observations.proposed_value: The gods, having come for amṛta, deliberate on Meru. Nārāyaṇa tells Brahmā that gods and asuras should churn the ocean (kalaśodadhi), which will yield amṛta with all herbs and gems
observations.note: The text has Nārāyaṇa's advice but no explicit resolution by the gods. The churning starts in the next section. The asuras' part in the churning, given in the advice, is left out of the old value.
